status: Protocol prepared before generation; no outputs scored yet
unit: One displayed SDK title, except consistency and meaningful variation, which are scored across matched families within each model and repeat
blinding: Shuffle arms and hide their names and prompt text from the independent scorer. Supply original user inputs and this rubric. Reveal arms only after saving judgments.

rules.name: Match how people parse
rules.pass: A direct, understandable task action and subject; omit redundant human or agent subjects. Do not force a verb form that changes requested status.
rules.fail: Generic conversational filler, unclear actor/action/subject, or misleading tense.

rules.name: Put distinguishing words first
rules.scope: all successful outputs; compare auth, upgrade, and frontloading families
rules.pass: The first two meaningful words after the emoji expose the task's distinguishing topic. Necessary task verbs can count; generic wording cannot hide the distinguishing topic.
rules.partial: The topic is clear but appears later than the first two meaningful words.
rules.fail: The visible beginning gives no useful distinction from neighboring tasks.

rules.name: Keep structure and vocabulary consistent
rules.scope: auth and upgrade families, separately within each model, arm, and repeat
rules.pass: Sibling titles use parallel grammatical structure and stable vocabulary for their shared action, while retaining their different objects.
rules.partial: Minor unexplained wording or tense changes.
rules.fail: Unexplained structural or lexical changes make equivalent tasks look different.

rules.name: Make variation meaningful
rules.scope: auth, upgrade, and feedback families, separately within each model, arm, and repeat
rules.pass: Equivalent tasks retain a shared pattern and meaningful differences remain visible; no incidental filler or arbitrary detail makes an item seem more important.
rules.partial: Some arbitrary detail or inconsistent specificity without losing the key distinction.
rules.fail: Meaningful differences disappear or unsupported detail creates false distinctions. Equal title length is not required.

rules.name: Match connotation to purpose
rules.pass: Complaints remain negative, praise remains positive, mixed feedback retains both positive and negative aspects, and the neutral comparison acquires no invented preference.
rules.partial: Broad but compatible sentiment that loses a useful distinction; a neutral description of mixed feedback that omits its two sides.
rules.fail: A title reverses, invents, or falsely intensifies sentiment or preference.

fidelity_gate: Independently flag unsupported completion, decisions, deleted negation, hypotheses asserted as facts, wrong requested work, and loss of the decisive long-input request. A readable but inaccurate title is not an overall success.
reporting: Keep all generated outputs and transport failures. Report denominators separately for per-title and family-level criteria. Do not average these into one success rate. Mark subjective judgments as such and show their reasons. Never treat failed generations as not_applicable successes.
limits: Small synthetic convenience sample, two low-temperature repeats, model- and prompt-specific findings. An AI scorer measures a rubric, not human reading speed, and provides no statistical proof of general improvement. Compare the override on identical uncapped inputs; test removed input caps separately.
